name: Lua
note: Lua keeps the OrdersController and OrderService in separate files, one file for each role. A Lua class is a global table: `OrdersController = {}`. Its methods are `function OrdersController:get_orders()`. Lua has no annotations, so Tachyon reads comment markers: `-- @RequestRoute("/orders")` on the controller table and `-- @GetRoute` on its method declare GET /orders. `-- @Public` says that anyone may call its routes; every route must say who may call it. `-- @Needs` on a field of the table asks Tachyon to fill `order_service` with the OrderService. LuaCATS comments (`---@class`, `---@field`, `---@type`, `---@return`) give every field and return value a type. Tachyon checks each file that you write. Then it joins the roles that use the same language and adds the protocol runtime. The protocol runtime is the code that passes requests and responses between the server and your route. Lua also writes Tac services in the same form, `client/services/TallyService.lua`, which run in the page on Tachyon's Lua WebAssembly runtime (ADR 0085). JSON `null` inside a list reads as `YonNull`, so the other items keep their places, and a `null` argument or field reads as `nil`. An empty JSON object stays an object.
